251202255.accepts_evidence: The foundation page tells organizations to confirm they meet the criteria, offers an online eligibility quiz, and directs them to the designated PNC representative for their region; it adds that requests exceed available funding (https://www.pnc.com/en/about-pnc/corporate-responsibility/philanthropy/pnc-foundation.html).
251202255.conflicts_with_return: The return points to www.givingprograms.com/pnc for guidelines; the current information is on pnc.com, so the address on the return is out of date. Otherwise none (open application, no fixed deadline).
251202255.contact: Regional designated representatives are listed by state and region on the foundation page (name, email, address, phone); no single national grants contact.
251202255.eligibility: Organizations with a current IRS tax-exempt designation that can receive charitable contributions. Grow Up Great grants must support early education for children birth to five, serve a majority of children from low- and moderate-income families, and include direct services, educator development or family engagement.
251202255.geographic_limits: The activity must take place in a community where PNC has a significant presence; eligible counties are listed by state and region on the page.
251202255.how_to_apply: Take the online eligibility quiz (CyberGrants) linked from the foundation page, then contact the designated PNC representative for your region, whose name, email and phone are listed by region on the same page.
251202255.name: PNC Foundation
251202255.not_funded: Organizations that discriminate; religious organizations except for non-sectarian activities; advocacy groups; operating funds for agencies that receive PNC United Way allocations; individuals; private foundations; annual funds for hospitals, colleges or universities; conferences and seminars; tickets and goodwill advertising.
251202255.notes: The first step for any client is checking whether its county is on PNC's list for its state, then finding the regional representative. Grow Up Great has a separate guidelines PDF, and Arts Alive runs regional cycles with their own applications; neither PDF was read here. PNC's charitable trusts (trusts PNC administers for others) are a separate page and separate funders.
251202255.page_dated: No date on the page; an Arts Alive application on the site is dated 2025.
priorities: education, with emphasis on early childhood education (PNC Grow Up Great, birth to age five)
economic development: affordable housing, community development, community services, arts and culture, neighborhood revitalization
PNC Arts Alive (regional arts initiative with its own guidelines)
251202255.types_of_support: Program grants in education and economic development; PNC also encourages employee volunteering in funded programs. Sponsorships are handled separately from the foundation.

251427015.accepts_evidence: The funding process page asks for a complete proposal package by mail or email ahead of two yearly board meetings, and says letters of intent are not processed. https://scaifefamily.org/our-funding-process
251427015.conflicts_with_return: None found; the return refers to an attachment for deadlines and restrictions.
251427015.contact: David Zywiec, President and Chairman; Scaife Family Foundation, 777 S. Flagler Drive, Suite 909 East Tower, West Palm Beach, FL 33401; (561) 659-1188. A submission email is on the page but is obscured and could not be read.
251427015.deadlines: February 1 for the annual spring board meeting; August 1 for the regular fall board meeting (no year shown); complete packages received earlier get priority
251427015.eligibility: Nonprofits with a current IRS 501(c)(3) determination whose request fits at least one focus area
251427015.geographic_limits: Not limited to one U.S. region; historically prioritizes South Florida and Western Pennsylvania
251427015.how_to_apply: Send a full package by U.S. mail or email: dated, signed proposal letter on letterhead (history, mission, purpose, amount, use of funds), IRS determination letter, operating budget and program budget if applicable, signed latest Form 990, board list, and latest audit and annual report. No portal.
251427015.name: Scaife Family Foundation
251427015.not_funded: Letters of intent; event sponsorship or endorsement proposals; requests for individuals
251427015.notes: Founded in Pittsburgh, now in West Palm Beach. Shares an office, phone, focus areas and an identical application process with the Jennie K. Scaife Charitable Foundation, a separate legal entity. Next deadline February 1, 2027. South Florida priority plus the women-and-children and addiction areas make this a direct fit for a South Florida women's program.
251427015.page_dated: not stated (copyright line has no year)
priorities: health and welfare of women and children
beneficial interaction between humans and animals; animal welfare
early intervention and prevention of drug and alcohol addiction
251427015.types_of_support: Operating or program support; the proposal letter must say which
